item.title: A Closer Examination of SCP-173:
item.content:encoded:
Well, I figured that since it's a very predictable object stored at the largest facility it's probably used a lot in training. Not particularly impressive, and not something that most people think about much once they're done training, but something that most people know about. Kind of like how everybody learns to play "Hot Cross Buns" on the recorder in music class, but you don't play it any more once you learn any actual songs or a real instrument.

That, and I figured its historical importance should warrant some kind of notoriety in-universe.

item.title: A Closer Examination of SCP-173:
item.content:encoded:
I don't particularly like the depiction of 173 as being a very well-known or famous object seeing how 173 seems to be rather mundane to me.

Other than that, I like it a lot.

item.title: SCP-5923:
item.content:encoded:
Yeah, I think you’re right, the inclusion of the village and -B in the description sorta deflates the discovery later on.

I've made that change, including the information about -A only once Rossi's experience has occurred and the Foundation has figured out there is a real town. I think it improves the pacing a lot.

Thanks!

item.title: SCP-5923:
item.content:encoded:
I find myself in the same place as Nico here, in that it's a competently written work that isn't quite satisfactory to me, though some of the sentence structuring threw me off a few more times than I would have liked. Obviously, that's a personal gripe, but it is what it is.

It feels like the parts that are stretched are all within setting the atmosphere, which while I appreciate, leaves the last log feeling a bit like retreading ground. I feel like a way to remedy that would be to have introduced -A later than within the initial phases of the description. I think having that come out later would allow for a more natural flow of establishing that the place is real, has a history of abandonment, and a reason to want more people to come through would pull the pieces a little tighter.

item.title: SCP-5358:
item.content:encoded:
In order for an article to work, there needs to be a strong narrative with a clear beginning, middle, and end. This has a beginning and a middle. There are no stakes, just a dude who is really good at something, and has no further character development other than that. It's boring and tasteless.

-1

item.title: SCP-3653:
item.content:encoded: The higher-ups are the only ones allowed to retain memory of the entire 527-day year. Everyone else is still present and conscious with their memories and experience during the rest of the year, and behaves as would be expected of them during these extra days, including upholding any responsibilities relating to containment. The SCPs are also subjected to this time loss, so it doesn't really give them any advantage.
